paper.abstract_en: Almost all solutions to vision tasks $\unicode{x2014}$ offered by nature and technology alike $\unicode{x2014}$ rely on capturing an image using a lens or a similar optical instrument, followed by computational analysis by neurons of a brain or a digital computer. This approach is inherently suboptimal in photon-limited and noisy conditions, where critical information is irreversibly lost at the measurement stage. We address this gap by introducing AI-driven optimization of quantum measurements on the incoming photons, learning how to extract the maximum possible information for a given computer vision task from each incoming photon. The trained measurement consists of a diffractive optical neural network (DONN) followed by a detector array. We train the DONN with a quantum information-theoretic objective that maximizes the rate at which the discrimination error decays as photons accumulate. The resulting measurement achieves exponentially lower error than both direct imaging and a DONN optimized for single-photon discrimination. We validate the advantage in a noiseless setting as well as a photon-counting experiment with an electron-multiplying CCD with the noise corresponding to $10^4$ photons per single signal photon, where the measurement also learns to mitigate the detector noise.
